skill.name: using-git-worktrees
skill.description: Set up isolated Git worktrees for feature work with directory selection, safety checks, project setup, and baseline test verification.
skill.summary: Create safe, isolated Git worktrees before starting implementation work.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline paths, and /dev/null redirects in a Git worktree guide. Contextual risk remains because the skill can automatically run dependency setup, trust CLAUDE.md for directory selection, and commit .gitignore changes. No prompt injection text or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Automatic dependency setup can execute untrusted project scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for explicit user approval before package installs, builds, or tests, and summarize the planned commands first.

remediation.issue: CLAUDE.md directory preferences are used without validation.
remediation.suggestion: Treat the value as untrusted data, restrict it to documented worktree locations, and ask before using unexpected paths.
Ask before creating commits, or stage the .gitignore change and wait for user approval.

static_findings.snippet: **If found:** Use that directory. If both exist, `.worktrees` wins.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Dependency Setup Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the assistant to run package installation and build commands when project files are detected. These commands can execute project-controlled lifecycle scripts or download dependencies before explicit review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 103-118 directly instruct automatic npm, cargo, pip, poetry, and go setup commands. These tools commonly execute project code or fetch packages, so the contextual risk is clear.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Repository Directory Preference
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the assistant to read CLAUDE.md for a worktree directory preference and use it without asking. A repository-controlled file could steer workspace creation to an unexpected path.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly say to grep CLAUDE.md and use a found preference without asking. The exact parsing behavior is not defined, so confidence is high enough to keep for author review.

content.value_statement: Feature work often needs a clean workspace without disrupting the current branch. This skill guides an assistant through safe Git worktree setup, project preparation, and baseline checks.
actual_capabilities: Checks for existing .worktrees or worktrees directories in priority order.
Looks for a repository worktree directory preference in CLAUDE.md.
Verifies project-local worktree directories are listed in .gitignore.
Creates a new Git worktree and branch for isolated feature work.
Detects common project files and runs matching setup commands.
Runs baseline tests and reports the worktree location and status.
limitations: Requires a Git repository that supports worktrees.
Needs permission before running shell commands in restricted environments.
Does not resolve dependency failures or test failures by itself.
May need user input when no preferred worktree directory exists.

use_cases.title: Start Feature Work Safely
use_cases.description: Create an isolated branch workspace before changing code, while preserving the current checkout.

use_cases.title: Prepare Implementation Tasks
use_cases.description: Set up dependencies and baseline tests before an assistant begins a planned implementation.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Worktree Conventions
use_cases.description: Follow existing repository preferences for worktree locations and ignore rules.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Worktree
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one feature branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an isolated Git worktree for my next feature. Follow the repository preference if one exists, then report the location.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Clean Baseline
prompt_templates.scenario: Setup with dependency and test verification.
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up a worktree for this task, install the detected project dependencies after confirming the commands, and run baseline tests.

prompt_templates.title: Use Repository Conventions
prompt_templates.scenario: Team project with existing worktree rules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a worktree using this repository's documented conventions. Validate the directory choice and .gitignore rule before creating it.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the Worktree Plan First
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced setup that needs a safety review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Before creating a worktree, show the selected directory, branch name, setup commands, and test commands. Wait for approval before making changes.

output_examples.input: Create a worktree for an authentication feature.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects the existing project worktree directory, verifies the ignore rule, creates an isolated branch workspace, and reports passing baseline tests.

output_examples.input: Prepare a worktree for a repository with no existing worktree directory.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks the user to choose between a project-local directory and a global configuration directory before proceeding.

output_examples.input: Start implementation after tests fail in the new worktree.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports the failing baseline tests and asks whether to investigate or continue with the known failure.

best_practices: Confirm generated setup and test commands before running them.
Keep project-local worktrees ignored by Git before creating them.
Record baseline test failures before starting implementation work.
anti_patterns: Creating worktrees in arbitrary paths without checking repository conventions.
Running dependency installation in untrusted repositories without review.
Proceeding after baseline test failures without user confirmation.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a Git worktree, which is a separate checkout linked to the same repository.

faq.question: Does it change my current branch?
faq.answer: It is designed to avoid changing the current checkout by doing feature work in a separate worktree.

faq.question: Why does it check .gitignore?
faq.answer: Project-local worktree folders should be ignored so generated workspace files are not accidentally committed.

faq.question: Can it run dependency installation?
faq.answer: Yes. The source instructions include detected setup commands, so users should approve those commands first.

faq.question: What happens if tests fail?
faq.answer: The skill directs the assistant to report the failures and ask before continuing.

faq.question: Is this only for Claude?
faq.answer: No. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
